subject: Jellyfin 12 contracts for (1) plugin dashboard configuration pages and the supported save/activation path, and (2) plugin logging with configurable verbosity (ADR-016 and ADR-020 gating)
conclusion: Both capabilities are supported through stable Jellyfin 12 APIs. A plugin exposes a dashboard settings page via IHasWebPages.GetPages()/PluginPageInfo, served by Jellyfin.Api DashboardController (web/ConfigurationPages, web/ConfigurationPage) from an embedded HTML resource, and saved through the elevation-gated PluginsController GET/POST {pluginId}/Configuration path into IHasPluginConfiguration.UpdateConfiguration. Activation is the plugin's responsibility: BasePlugin<T>.UpdateConfiguration persists the XML and raises ConfigurationChanged but does not refresh plugin runtime state, so ArrTags must override UpdateConfiguration (call base, then ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace) or subscribe to ConfigurationChanged. Logging uses ILogger<T>/ILoggerFactory resolved through plugin DI, which flows to the host Serilog log with the logger category as {SourceContext}. Per-plugin verbosity is only supported as plugin-owned gating from its own configuration; the host's Serilog MinimumLevel.Override is host configuration, not a plugin API, and a plugin-registered ILoggerProvider/sink is ineffective on the pinned host (Jellyfin calls the no-argument UseSerilog() with no LoggerProviderCollection). Adding logging creates a new secret-exposure path that the current SEC-5 negative result does not cover.

findings.claim: A plugin exposes a dashboard configuration page by implementing MediaBrowser.Model.Plugins.IHasWebPages with IEnumerable<PluginPageInfo> GetPages(); PluginPageInfo has Name, DisplayName, EmbeddedResourcePath, EnableInMainMenu, MenuSection, MenuIcon.
findings.source: MediaBrowser.Model/Plugins/IHasWebPages.cs and PluginPageInfo.cs at pinned revision; confirmed in MediaBrowser.Model.dll 12.0.0.0.

findings.claim: Jellyfin serves the page: DashboardController GET web/ConfigurationPages (RequiresElevation) lists IHasWebPages plugin pages, and GET web/ConfigurationPage?name= returns plugin.GetType().Assembly.GetManifestResourceStream(page.EmbeddedResourcePath) via MimeTypes.GetMimeType (.html -> text/html).

In the pinned source the page-resource action GetDashboardConfigurationPage carries no [Authorize]; DashboardController has no class-level [Authorize]; AddJellyfinApiAuthorization sets a DefaultPolicy but no FallbackPolicy. The static page resource is reachable without authentication. This is not a data boundary (static HTML/JS only); the configuration data endpoints are administrator-gated.
findings.classification: Internal implementation detail (route/authorization behavior), not live-confirmed

findings.claim: The supported configuration save path is PluginsController (class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)]): GET {pluginId}/Configuration returns IHasPluginConfiguration.Configuration; POST {pluginId}/Configuration deserializes the body with JsonDefaults.Options (PascalCase) and calls IHasPluginConfiguration.UpdateConfiguration.

BasePlugin<TConfigurationType>.UpdateConfiguration is virtual: it sets Configuration, calls SaveConfiguration(Configuration) (XML to ConfigurationFilePath = plugins/configurations/<file>), and raises ConfigurationChanged. It does not refresh plugin runtime state.

Activation must be wired by the plugin: override UpdateConfiguration to call base then ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace, or subscribe to ConfigurationChanged. BasePlugin<T>.Configuration is lazy-loaded and replaced, so a snapshot service built from plugin.Configuration does not observe later replacements unless wired. Plugin already receives IServiceProvider.

The README claim 'There is no web configuration UI in v1' is accurate for the current source: src/ArrTags has no IHasWebPages/GetPages/PluginPageInfo and no embedded HTML resource (only Resources/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf); configuration is read from plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml at startup (limitation F2).
findings.source: src/ArrTags source and csproj EmbeddedResource entries; docs/limitations.md F2.

findings.claim: The config-page mechanism is shape-identical between Jellyfin v10.9.11 and the pinned v12.0 revision; the 12-specific difference is the authorization pipeline (AddJellyfinApiAuthorization with the RequiresElevation administrator-role-claim policy), not the page mechanism.
findings.source: Pinned v12.0 DashboardController/PluginsController/PluginPageInfo vs the v10.9.11 GitHub equivalents.

findings.claim: ILogger<T>/ILoggerFactory are resolvable through plugin DI: plugin service registrators run before the provider is built (ApplicationHost.Init -> PluginManager.RegisterServices), and plugin controllers are added via AddControllersAsServices. Plugin log lines flow through the host Serilog pipeline to the console and %JELLYFIN_LOG_DIR%/log_.log sinks with {SourceContext} = logger category (by convention the type full name).

Host log level is Serilog configuration only: logging.default.json (bundled default) plus optional logging.json (LoggingConfigFileSystem), both reloadOnChange, plus JELLYFIN_-prefixed env/cmdline. MinimumLevel.Override is keyed by source-context prefix (e.g. "ArrTags": "Debug") but is host configuration, not a plugin API. ServerConfiguration has no log-level field; the dashboard exposes log viewing, not level control.
findings.classification: Confirmed supported API for the mechanism; MinimumLevel.Override keys are public but potentially unstable

findings.claim: A plugin can control its own verbosity independently and in a fully supported way by gating its own log calls from its own configuration snapshot (a bounded verbosity field validated with PluginConfiguration, read before calling _logger.LogDebug(...)). This has no host dependency and is the recommended mechanism.
findings.source: Standard Microsoft.Extensions.Logging usage; no host API required.

findings.claim: A plugin-registered ILoggerProvider/sink does not receive events on the pinned host: Jellyfin calls the no-argument UseSerilog(), registering ILoggerFactory as new SerilogLoggerFactory(null, false) with no LoggerProviderCollection; SerilogLoggerFactory.AddProvider ignores providers and CreateLogger always returns a Serilog logger. UseSerilog(writeToProviders: true) is not used.
findings.classification: Public but potentially unstable API; ineffective on the pinned host

findings.claim: src/ArrTags currently has zero logging call sites (no ILogger/Console./Debug.Write/Trace.Write/Log.*); the only ILogger<> references are test doubles. The docs claim 'no plugin log path can leak a secret' (SEC-5) is accurate today.

internal: host Serilog wiring (no-arg UseSerilog, SerilogLoggerFactory without provider collection)

risks: The config page resource endpoint is anonymous in the pinned source (static HTML/JS only; data endpoints are admin-gated) and was not live-confirmed.
Adding logging creates a new secret-exposure path; PluginConfiguration contains Sonarr.ApiKey, Radarr.ApiKey, and WebhookSecret.
Plugin-registered ILoggerProvider is silently ignored (host-internal Serilog wiring); a plugin must not rely on it.
logging.json vs logging.user.json filename inconsistency exists in the pinned revision; confirm on a live host only if relying on host per-category overrides.
jellyfin-web client loading/CSP behavior is not pinned by the server repository.
System.Text.Json population of ArrTags get-only Collection<T> config properties (EnabledLibraries, Renderer.Selectors) on the POST round-trip is unverified.
documentation_impact: docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md (new section 9 'Plugin configuration pages (Jellyfin 12)' and section 10 'Plugin logging and log levels (Jellyfin 12)'; extended section 8 Source references)
ADR-016 and ADR-020 (consumers only; not created here)
recommended_action: ADR-016: implement IHasWebPages with an embedded Configuration/config.html (logical name ArrTags.Configuration.config.html), use the elevation-gated PluginsController save path, and override Plugin.UpdateConfiguration to call ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace (surfacing validation failure safely). ADR-020: log through ILogger<T> and gate verbosity with a plugin-owned, bounded, secret-free configuration field; do not register a custom logging provider/sink; require every log call site to be secret-free and add redaction tests plus a security review of SEC-5.
unresolved: ADR-016: accept the anonymous page-resource endpoint (static HTML/JS) or live-confirm route/authorization on the pinned host.
ADR-016: verify System.Text.Json populates ArrTags get-only Collection<T> configuration properties on POST.
ADR-016: decide read-only vs read/write page and how TryReplace validation failure is surfaced through Dashboard.processPluginConfigurationUpdateResult.
ADR-020: choose plugin-owned verbosity vs host MinimumLevel.Override and fix the logger category/prefix convention (for example ArrTags.*).
ADR-020: if host per-category overrides are relied on, confirm the effective override filename (logging.json vs logging.user.json) and reload behavior on a live pinned host.
No live-host probe was performed for either question; conclusions are from pinned assemblies and version-pinned sources.
